quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 35

questions.question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of their way.
questions.explanation: When you see an aggressive driver, the safest choice is to move out of their way. Do not try to compete with other drivers.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Yield sign ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a yield sign is coming. Start to slow down when you see this warning.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead has curves.

questions.question: This white sign means you should not pass other vehicles:

options.text: Until after you pass the sign.
Unless it seems safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: For any reason.
questions.explanation: White rectangular signs show rules you must follow. This sign means you cannot pass other vehicles under any circumstances.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Lane reduction. The right lane ends soon and traffic should merge left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lane reduction. The right lane ends soon and traffic should merge left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that there will be fewer lanes ahead. Traffic must move to the left lane.

questions.question: This sign shows one type of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that your road ends at an intersection ahead. Slow down and prepare to stop or turn.

questions.question: This sign tells you that:

options.text: No turns are allowed on the road.
There is a series of curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a series of curves ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers that the road has curves coming up.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for bicycles.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They warn drivers to watch for bicycles and other road users crossing.

questions.question: As you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Wait for a green light before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, look for other traffic, and then proceed carefully.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Side road.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a side road is ahead.

questions.question: A blood alcohol concentration of 0.02 percent:

options.text: Won't put other drivers at risk.
Doubles your chances of having an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Doubles your chances of having an accident.
questions.explanation: Every 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol concentration nearly doubles a driver's risk of a fatal crash.

questions.question: A solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal means:

options.text: Speed up to make the turn before the light changes.
You don't need to signal when turning from that lane.
Get ready to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the green arrow is ending. You should get ready to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before turning.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: Use your left foot to brake.
Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
Always brake hard to ensure you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
questions.explanation: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating. Apply the brakes gently with increasing pressure so your vehicle stops gradually and smoothly.

questions.question: Fatigue increases the risk of:

options.text: Falling asleep at the wheel and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep at the wheel and crashing.
questions.explanation: Fatigue causes mistakes in speed and distance judgment. It slows your decision-making and increases crash risk. You could fall asleep at the wheel and crash, hurting or killing yourself or others.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that wet pavement is slippery and dangerous. It can cause you to lose control. Slow down on wet roads because it takes longer to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downgrade ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep downgrade is ahead. Check your brakes.

questions.question: To avoid skidding on slippery surfaces, you should:

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.
Speed up entering curves and slow down exiting them.
Slow down before entering curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve because you don't know what's ahead. Braking on a curve may cause you to skid.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic merging from the right.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions ahead. This sign tells you to be ready for traffic merging from the right.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light at an intersection means:

options.text: The same as a yield sign.
The light is about to turn green.
The same as a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and go when it's safe. This is the same as a stop sign.

questions.question: You are driving on the freeway behind a large truck. How should you drive?

options.text: Drive close behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see farther ahead.
Drive farther behind the truck than you would behind a regular car.
Drive no more than one car length behind the truck so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive farther behind the truck than you would behind a regular car.
questions.explanation: If you drive too close behind a truck, the truck driver cannot see you in their mirrors. This is dangerous because you lose your safety distance if the truck stops suddenly.

questions.question: The road ahead is flooded with water. What should you do?

options.text: Do not drive through the water. Turn around and find another route.
Drive through the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive through the water. Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive through flooded roads. The water may hide dangers even if it looks shallow. Find a different route to your destination.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road splits. You must go right or left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road splits. You must go right or left.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black markings. This sign warns you that the road splits and you must choose to go right or left.

questions.question: You see this yellow sign. What should you do?

options.text: Stop at the crosswalk until a crossing guard signals you to go.
Be ready to stop if children are in the crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if children are in the crosswalk.
questions.explanation: A five-sided sign means a school is nearby. Stay alert and stop if children are crossing.

questions.question: On a slippery road, what following distance should you keep?

options.text: Farther away from the car ahead than normal.
Closer to the car ahead than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away from the car ahead than normal.
questions.explanation: You need more distance to stop on a slippery road than on a dry road. Always increase your following distance on slippery roads.

questions.question: Which statement is true about railroad crossings?

options.text: Use cruise control near railroad crossings to maintain a constant speed.
Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
You have the right-of-way at railroad crossings and do not need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
questions.explanation: You must stop at railroad crossings when a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal tells you to. Be careful near railroad tracks.

questions.question: At a school crossing sign, what should you do?

options.text: Always stop, even if there is no stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk your horn when you see children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Five-sided signs mean you are near a school or school crossing. Be alert and prepare to stop.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign prohibits U-turns. You cannot turn around to go in the opposite direction where this sign is posted.

questions.question: When may you pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a road with a solid line next to your lane.
On a road with a broken line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a road with a broken line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken line means you can cross it to change lanes. When a yellow line is dashed on your side, you may pass. When it is solid on your side, you may not pass. Only change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: A sharp right turn is ahead.
A road joins from the right.
The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black markings. This sign warns you that the road will turn sharply right and then sharply left.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road is changing direction or getting narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is changing direction or getting narrower.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead is changing direction or getting narrower. You will see these signs on sharp curves or near narrow bridges.

questions.question: A driving distraction is:

options.text: Anything that makes you swerve while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you pay more attention to driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: A driving distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving. Distractions can happen anytime and anywhere. Distracted driving can cause crashes that result in property damage, injury, or death.

questions.question: When driving near a large truck or bus, you should:

options.text: Follow it closely to reduce wind resistance on your vehicle.
Avoid staying beside it for long periods.
Drive on its right side when going around curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid staying beside it for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large trucks and buses have large blind spots on both sides. Do not stay beside them for a long time.

questions.question: In heavy fog, you should slow down and:
questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beams when driving in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off water droplets and create glare, making it harder to see. Some cars have fog lights that you can use along with low beams.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Watch for vehicles that are required to stop at railroad crossings, like school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials.
Watch for trains coming from multiple directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with extreme caution. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. Be aware of vehicles that must stop at railroad crossings, such as school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials.

questions.question: A "No passing zone" sign tells drivers:

options.text: That passing is not safe in this area.
To drive at a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: That passing is not safe in this area.
questions.explanation: A "No passing zone" sign means you cannot pass another vehicle in that area. It is illegal and unsafe to pass because you cannot see far enough ahead.

questions.question: Before entering an intersection, you should look:

options.text: Left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look both left and right for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians. Look left a second time because vehicles from your left will be closer and more dangerous. Check across the intersection to make sure it is clear.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ending.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns that the divided highway is ending. Be ready to change lanes or adjust your position.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Be ready for traffic to merge into your lane from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for traffic to merge into your lane from the right.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns that traffic from the right will be merging into your lane. Be prepared to let them merge safely.

questions.question: If you must stop on a freeway shoulder due to an emergency, you should:

options.text: Raise your hood and stay in your car while waiting for help.
Stand behind your car to warn other drivers.
Get out of your car and walk to find help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Raise your hood and stay in your car while waiting for help.
questions.explanation: Stopping on a freeway shoulder is dangerous and only allowed in emergencies. Raise your hood and turn on your hazard lights to show you have a problem. Do not walk along the freeway to look for help.
